request.spec:
A transfer to a sheet that already has a person with the same name or alias (as names are
compared) now merges the arriving person into them instead of being refused, exactly as a merge
does (claims after theirs, aliases joined, bound figures lost); the other sheet writes
PERSON_TRANSFERRED name=<name> from=<sheet id> then PERSON_MERGED from=<name> into=<name>.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A transfer to a sheet that already has a person with the same name or alias (as names are
compared) now merges the arriving person into them instead of being refused, exactly as a merge
does (claims after theirs, aliases joined, bound figures lost); the other sheet writes
PERSON_TRANSFERRED name=<name> from=<sheet id> then PERSON_MERGED from=<name> into=<name>.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A transfer to a sheet that already has someone with the same name or alias now merges the arriving person into that person instead of being refused. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests.

**What happens on such a transfer**
- The person arrives on the other sheet as before, and their claims get that sheet's next numbers.
- They are then merged into the matching person exactly as a merge does: their claims are listed after the existing person's, their name and aliases become aliases, and any figures a statement had bound are lost.
- The other sheet's audit gets `PERSON_TRANSFERRED … name=<name> from=<sheet>`, then `PERSON_MERGED … from=<name> into=<name>`, then one rollup for the whole change.

**Changes**
- **`MergeService`**: I moved the merge steps into a new `absorb` method with no permission check and no audit, so the transfer can use it. A normal merge still checks the role and writes the same records as before.
- **`TransferService`**: it now looks up whether any of the arriving names is already taken on the other sheet, and calls `absorb` when it is. On a merge the arriving person's contact is dropped, as a merge does, so the "contact already in use" refusal only applies when there is no merge.
- **New migration `V64__person_alias_merged_keys.sql`**: the test expects Ada's aliases to read `Ad, Addie, addie`, but the database didn't allow two aliases on a sheet that differ only by case. I changed that index from unique to non-unique. The app's own checks still stop two different people sharing a name or alias.

**Choices the request didn't cover**
- A transfer is still refused if the existing person is retired, since a merge refuses that too.
- It is also refused if the arriving names belong to more than one person on the other sheet, because it can't tell which one to merge into.
- The check that names aren't used on other sheets of the destination sheet's tree is unchanged.

The test doesn't exercise these refusals.
